title: Battery Replacement Warranties: Battery Tests as the Evidence of Warranty Decisions
content:
Battery and charging-system tests are free at any Crestline store for a battery covered by the Battery Replacement Warranties, and they are the evidence of every warranty decision. Each test is recorded with its printed result, the measured cold cranking amps and the battery's whole months in service.

## Policy

(a) **Charge and retest.** A battery testing charge and retest is charged, at the line's recharge service charge, and tested again before any decision, and only the retest counts.

(b) **Failure.** A fully charged battery fails when the tester shows replace or bad cell, or when the measured cold cranking amps are at or below the line's failure threshold percentage of its rated cold cranking amps.

(c) **Charging system.** Where the line requires a charging-system test, the alternator and starter are tested on the same visit. A charging system fault result means the battery failure is not decided until the fault is repaired.

(d) **Age of the evidence.** A warranty decision may rest only on a test no older than the line's test validity period in calendar days.

## Results and what they settle

| Printed result or reading of a fully charged battery | Effect |
|---|---|
| replace | the battery fails |
| bad cell | the battery fails |
| measured cold cranking amps at or below the line's threshold percentage of its rated cold cranking amps | the battery fails |
| charge and retest | the battery is charged and tested again; the first result does not count and only the retest counts |
| charging system fault | the battery failure is not decided until the fault is repaired |

## Worked threshold, on hypothetical figures

*Hypothetical, not any line's figures:* a battery rated at 500 cold cranking amps with a 70% threshold. 70% of 500 is 350. A fully charged battery measuring 350 fails, being at the threshold; one measuring 351 does not fail on cold cranking amps, and whether it fails then turns on the printed result.

## Points of judgement

- *Does the first reading of a battery that tests charge and retest settle the claim?* No; only the retest counts.
- *Can a test from an earlier visit support a decision?* Only if it is no older than the line's test validity period.
- *Can a failure be decided while the charging-system test shows a fault?* No; it is not decided until the fault is repaired.
